subject: free-tailed bat
title: These Bats Jam Each Other's Sonar to Make Rivals Miss

scenes.text: These bats sabotage each other's hunts without ever touching.
Mexican free-tailed bats hunt moths in total darkness, by sonar.
Right before a catch, a hunting bat fires a rapid burst of calls to lock on.
That's the moment a rival answers with a strange, wobbling siren call.
It jams the hunter's sonar. In tests, a well-timed call foiled up to 86 percent of catches.
Scientists think it's food theft. No claws, no bites. Just noise.

description:
Mexican free-tailed bats jam the sonar of rival bats at the exact moment they close in on a moth.
In a Wake Forest University study published in Science, a well-timed jamming call foiled up to 86 percent of capture attempts.
What other animal do you think fights with sound?
first_comment: Mexican free-tailed bats have about 15 different calls, and only this one seems to exist purely for sabotage. Which animal would you want on your team?
